steps: Trim hard white fat from beef. Cut remaining meat into ½" cubes. Toss w 2 pinches salt & 3T oil.
Spread in even layer on sheet tray. Broil 6" from heating element til milk chocolate brown, 6-12 min, checking periodically.
Add 3 T olive oil to large pot over medium heat. Sweat onion with pinch of salt, about 6 min. Add garlic, cook 60 sec. Add tomato paste & butter. Melt, fry for 1 min til rusty red.
Stir in flour. Cook 30 sec until no lumps. Add wine & Guinness, scraping bottom. Bring to simmer, cook 3 min.
Whisk gelatin into stock. Add stock mixture to pot along with BTB & Worcestershire. Stir, bring to a simmer.
Add broiled beef with all drippings & carrots. Return to simmer. Add sachet of thyme and bay. Cover, braise in 300°F / 150°C oven 80-95 mins
Check a cube of beef for doneness. Let the stew cool slightly then refrigerate overnight.

The next day, spoon off most of the hardened fat, discard. Gently reheat until the liquid melts. Remove sachet. Remove beef and carrots, draining well. Bring sauce to a simmer uncovered over medium high and reduce for 15–20 minutes, stirring frequently. Taste for seasoning and adjust with salt if needed.
Gently fold the beef and carrots back into the sauce. Cool uncovered.

To Make the dough: In a large food processor, pulse flour, salt, sugar. Add cold, diced cream cheese, pulse about 15 times. Add cold cubed butter. Pulse 10-15 times to incorporate. Remove lid, add water then 1 egg and 1 egg yolk evenly over the top of the dry mixture. Add lid and pulse several more times to incorporate, scraping the bowl halfway through
Divide in six 200g portions, flatten into thick rectangles, wrap, and refrigerate for 20–30 minutes.
To Assemble: Lightly flour both sides of a rectangle of dough androlling pin. Roll 3–4 times, rotate 90 degrees, flip, and repeat until about 1/8 inch thick and measures approximately 10” x 8”

Use 7 oz ramekin as guide, cut a circle that’s about 1 inches wider than the ramekin on all sides. Directly next to first cut out, use the upside-down ramekin to mark and cut a smaller circle for the lid.

Press larger circle into a greased ramekin, eliminating air pockets. Add 200g cooled filling, pressing to eliminate voids. Top with the smaller circle and pinch to seal tightly. Create a vent in the center of the dough lid. Brush with egg wash.
Place pies on a sheet tray in a 425°F / 220°C oven for 28–33 minutes, until deeply golden brown
Rest 10 minutes before serving
